```python
def left_rotate(n, d):
    d %= 32
    mask = 0xFFFFFFFF
    n &= mask
    return ((n << d) | (n >> (32 - d))) & mask

assert left_rotate(16, 2) == 64
```

The team note says a plain left shift is enough. That's only true when no set bits reach the top of the 32-bit word. A real rotation has to wrap those bits around to the low end, for example `left_rotate(0x80000000, 1)` should give 1. My version does that, and it gives the same results as a plain shift whenever nothing wraps, so it also passes `left_rotate(16, 2) == 64`.
